habitat: Singly or in pairs in a variety of habitats, including suburbia. It roosts and breeds in large trees, caves, buildings and Hamerkop nests.
summary: A common resident. A pale, slim owl with a whitish heart-shaped facial disc and whitish spotted underparts. The upperparts are grey and tawny and spotted, paler than African Grass Owl. The call is an eerie wavering screech. The Kemp name Barn Owl and the code VB were left unchanged.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. Grey and tawny are both named for the upperparts, so no single back colour is stored. The grade A call is from the Western Cape. The Kemp name Barn Owl and the code VB were left unchanged.
